## The condensate borrow {#sec-ch08-borrow}

### Summary

A negative condensate is repaired by moving the deficit out of the parent vapour of the same cell. The
condensate is set to exactly zero and the total mass of the cell does not change. It is the one repair of
this chapter that conserves mass, and it conserves elements when the nucleation reaction is mass-balanced.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Repair a negative condensate by borrowing the deficit from its parent vapour in the same cell.

**Data.** In: the interior species rows of `hydro_u` and the parent metadata of each cloud. Out: the rows repaired in place.

**Placement.** Inside the conserved pass of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter, after the floors and before the column repair.

**Activation.** With the limiter, for clouds that carry parent-vapour metadata; a parentless cloud is skipped.

**Guarantee / limits.** Conserves the cell's mass to round-off; elements only for a mass-balanced reaction; vapour may go negative.

**Evidence.** `[C3]`, `[C8]` of `floors_check`; no ctest isolates the borrow.
:::

Local symbols: $d_{\mathrm c}$ [kg m$^{-3}$] is the deficit of a cloud, its negative part; $f_n$ the cached
fraction of parent $n$ and $N_{\mathrm{par}}$ the number of parents. $\nu_{nk}$[^rg-cb136b31be5a], $\mu_n$[^rg-ee4e75c3819a], $\rho_n$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$[^rg-5922fe4a6c9d] are
defined in @sec-appa.

### Derivation

A negative condensate does not mean mass is missing. It means the tracer flux over-drained the cell and
the mass is in a neighbour. Clamping it to zero invents that mass, one way, every time.

The alternative the code takes is to move mass between rows of the same cell. It takes the deficit out of the parent
vapours and sets the condensate to exactly zero. A cloud's parents are the vapour reactants of the first nucleation
reaction that produces it, possibly several, and each gets the cached fraction

$$
f_n = \frac{\nu_{nk}\,\mu_n}{\sum_{m}\nu_{mk}\,\mu_m} , \qquad \sum_n f_n = 1 ,
$$ {#eq-ch08-borrow-fractions}

with the sums over the $N_{\mathrm{par}}$ parents $n$ of reaction $k$[^rg-7d2ed75f8ca7] (`parent_mass`,
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}}). A deficit $d_{\mathrm c}<0$ adds
$d_{\mathrm c}f_n$ to parent $n$ and removes $d_{\mathrm c}$ from the cloud, so the cell total changes by
$d_{\mathrm c}\sum_n f_n - d_{\mathrm c} = 0$. The conservation comes
from the normalisation, not from the phases (`[C8]`). The elements are conserved as well only if the reaction is
mass-balanced, so that the parents' $\sum_n\nu_{nk}\mu_n$ is the cloud's molar mass times its coefficient; the code
does not check that.

`[C3]` measures the difference rather than asserting it. Over two thousand cells with a negative condensate, clamping
to zero adds $3.770\times10^{-2}$ of mass, while the borrow changes the total by exactly $0$ [check
`src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.out`]. The code comment at
`parentless` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) records the
motivation from a measurement. The clamp was responsible for $102\%$ of the total-mass drift in silicate cloud runs.
That number comes from a run this chapter cites rather than reproduces.

### Numerical method

The repair is `parent_slot`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). For each cloud row with
parent metadata, the deficit is the negative part at `clamp_max`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). It is added to each parent
vapour in proportion to its mass fraction at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}, and the condensate is then
set to exactly zero.

Two conditions are worth noting. A cloud not produced by nucleation has no parent metadata and is skipped, flagged for
the column repair of @sec-ch08-fixvapor instead. And the repair is purely local, so a ghost cell that holds a copy of
the same state receives the identical repair without any communication. That is what keeps ranks consistent.

**Why borrowing, and what it costs.** Three facts of the code and one bound.

1. The deficit is the negative part of the condensate, added to each parent vapour in proportion to its mass fraction.
   The condensate is then set to exactly zero
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
2. The repair is per cell, so a ghost cell holding a copy of the same state receives the identical repair with no
   communication.
3. A cloud without nucleation metadata has no parent and is flagged for the column repair of @sec-ch08-fixvapor.
4. With $N_{\mathrm{par}}$ parents the cell total changes only by rounding: $\sum_n f_n$ is one to within
   $N_{\mathrm{par}}$ roundings, and each addition rounds its product and its sum, so to first order the change is at
   most $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\bigl((N_{\mathrm{par}}+1)\lvert d_{\mathrm c}\rvert + \sum_n\rho_n\bigr)$, with
   $\rho_n$ the repaired parent densities. `[C3]` measures exactly $0$ for one parent; `[C8]` at most $0.92$ of the bound for one to four.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| the motivation, measured | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} | `clamp_min_` | |
| the repair | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} | `parentless` | clouds with parents |
| the deficit | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} | `deficit` | |
| borrowing from the parents | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} | `parent_slot` | |

: Code map of the condensate borrow. {#tbl-ch08-borrow-code}

**How to use it.** There is no switch of its own. The borrow runs inside the conserved pass whenever the limiter is on
and the thermodynamics declares clouds with parents. The repair is these lines
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}):

```cpp
      auto deficit = c.clamp_max(0.);
      for (auto const& [parent_slot, mass_fraction] : parents) {
        cons[parent_slot] += deficit * mass_fraction;
      }
      c.clamp_min_(0.);  // condensate to exactly zero
```

`c` is one cloud row on the interior, `deficit` its negative part, and `parents` the parent rows with their
mass fractions.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| this chapter's check | `[C3]` the borrow conserves mass where a clamp invents it; `[C8]` with several parents, through the normalised fractions | exact; round-off | the check's own bounds: `floors_check.py` `check_C3` asserts the borrow's total-mass drift below $10^{-18}$ over 2000 cells; `check_C8` asserts the derived round-off bound |

: Tests of the condensate borrow. {#tbl-ch08-borrow-tests}

The chapter's check compares the borrow with a clamp on synthetic cells.[^ch08-borrow-run] `[C3]`: over 2000
cells with a negative condensate, clamping to zero adds $3.770\times10^{-2}$ of mass while the borrow changes
the total by exactly $0$, and no cell went vapour-negative. `[C8]`: over 2000 cells with one to four parents the
total changes by at most $0.92$ of the bound, while the same additions with the un-normalised weights $\nu_{nk}\mu_n$
change it by up to $1.95\times10^{-4}$. No ctest isolates the borrow: **missing evidence**
for a snapy run.

[^ch08-borrow-run]: [sha: snapy@ccf40f9565642c32be69f4b9ef0cfa6daff3f201; deck: the check itself, synthetic numpy
    states; run: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process; Python 3.14.7, numpy 2.5.1;
    output identical to the committed file]. Output
    `floors_check.out`, lines `[C3]` and `[C8]`.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A cell whose vapour cannot cover the deficit goes vapour-negative. The borrow does not fail there; it
  hands the problem to the column repair, which may itself fail.
:::

1. **The phase shift is not free.** The repair moves mass between phases. The code comment puts that at about one per
   cent of the local value and expects the saturation adjustment to re-equilibrate within the same cycle. That
   expectation is a hypothesis recorded in the code; no test in the repository measures the residual phase error after
   the adjustment.
2. **Not provided:** the prevalence of clouds without nucleation metadata; this chapter describes the
   borrow rule rather than surveying simulation inputs. Such clouds get no borrow at all.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-cb136b31be5a]: $\nu_{nk}$ — stoichiometric coefficient of species $n$ in reaction $k$, always with both indices; never bare $\nu$, which is kinematic viscosity (§8)

[^rg-ee4e75c3819a]: $\mu_n$ — molar mass of species $n$ [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $\mu_{\mathrm{d}}$ for dry air. Never bare $\mu$, which is dynamic viscosity (§8); the code stores the inverse

[^rg-5922fe4a6c9d]: $\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}}$ — machine epsilon of the working precision (never bare $\epsilon$, which is $\epsilon_{\mathrm{piv}}$); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L11-L14)

[^rg-7d2ed75f8ca7]: $k = 1..N_r$ — reaction index and the number of reactions; never the $x_3$ cell index $k$ (§1) — a chapter that needs both renames the reaction index to $\varkappa$ and says so
